news.title: STEM Kids Championship 5th Edition: Registration Now Open
news.excerpt: Registration for the 5th Edition of the STEM Kids Championship has officially commenced. Schools registering 10 candidates or more can take advantage of an Early Bird fee of ₦2,000 per candidate.
news.author: Prime STEM Nigeria
body: We are excited to announce the official commencement of registration for the 5th Edition of the STEM Kids Championship. This edition promises to be bigger, more competitive and more rewarding for participating schools, teachers and candidates.

The championship gives young learners across Africa a platform to demonstrate their knowledge, develop confidence and compete in a stimulating academic environment — while building a strong foundation in Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics.

EARLY BIRD REGISTRATION OFFER: Schools registering 10 candidates or more can take advantage of our special Early Bird registration fee of just ₦2,000 per candidate. This offer is available for only a few days, so schools are encouraged to register early and secure this special rate.
PAYMENT DETAILS — Account Name: Prime STEM Nigeria. Account Number: 1025357212. Bank: United Bank for Africa (UBA).

PREPARE TO COMPETE. PREPARE TO WIN. To help candidates prepare effectively, we have also released the STEM Kids Championship Master Preparatory Guide. The comprehensive guide contains general strategies for preparing for and winning academic competitions, recommended topics to study, four years of comprehensive past questions and answers (2022–2025), and useful guidance to help candidates understand the competition and prepare with confidence.

The STEM Kids Championship is more than a competition — it is an opportunity for young learners to challenge themselves, develop critical thinking skills, gain valuable experience and earn recognition among some of the brightest young STEM minds.
Inspiring Young Minds. Building Africa's STEM Future.

news.title: Celebrating Excellence: 2025 Nigerian STEM Championship Awards Ceremony
news.excerpt: Outstanding young scientists, coders and chemists from across Nigeria were celebrated at the 2025 awards ceremony in partnership with Prime STEM Nigeria.
news.author: AFRISTEM Team
body: The 2025 Nigerian STEM Championship Awards Ceremony brought together students, parents, teachers, school leaders and partners to celebrate a year of remarkable achievement in Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics.

Winners of the STEM Kids Championship, the African Organic Chemistry Tournament and the Annual National Science Championship received certificates, trophies and prizes recognising their dedication and excellence.

"What we celebrate today is not just knowledge, but curiosity, resilience and the courage to compete," the organisers noted during the ceremony. "These young people represent the future of African innovation."
AFRISTEM extends its gratitude to every participating school, every teacher who prepared their students, and our partners whose support made the ceremony possible.

news.title: Why Science Spelling Builds Confident Scientists
news.excerpt: Scientific vocabulary is the language of discovery. Here is how SciSPELL turns intimidating terminology into an exciting, memorable learning experience.
news.author: AFRISTEM Team
body: Every scientific discipline has its own language. From 'photosynthesis' to 'mitochondria' to 'electronegativity', the words students encounter in textbooks can feel like barriers — or they can become keys that unlock understanding.
SciSPELL was designed around a simple insight: when students master the vocabulary of science, they gain confidence to engage with the concepts behind the words.

Beyond spelling, participants learn etymology, definitions and context. They stand before an audience, listen carefully, think under pressure and communicate clearly — skills that serve them far beyond the competition stage.
Schools that have taken part report students returning to class more curious, more articulate, and more willing to ask questions. That is exactly the outcome SciSPELL was built to create.

news.title: From Consumers to Creators: The Vision Behind Code Africa
news.excerpt: Young Africans are among the world's most enthusiastic technology users. Code Africa exists to help them become its builders.
news.author: AFRISTEM Team
body: Africa has the youngest population on earth, and its young people are embracing technology at an extraordinary pace. But using technology and creating with it are two very different things.
Code Africa is a pan-African coding competition built to close that gap. It challenges students to think computationally, solve real problems and build working solutions — often for the first time.
Participating schools gain more than a competition entry. They gain a reason to start a coding club, train a teacher, and give students a platform to showcase what they can build.
As the competition grows across borders, it is also building something bigger: a network of young African coders who know each other, learn from each other and will one day build together.

news.title: How Your School Can Start a Thriving STEM Club
news.excerpt: A practical, step-by-step guide for school leaders and teachers who want to bring hands-on STEM into their school — even on a tight budget.
news.author: AFRISTEM Team
body: You don't need a state-of-the-art laboratory to start a STEM club. You need a committed teacher, a regular time slot, and a few well-chosen activities that make students want to come back.
Start small: one afternoon a week, a simple challenge (build the tallest paper tower, program a simple game, extract DNA from a strawberry), and a culture where trying and failing is celebrated.

Connect the club to something bigger. Registering for a competition like SciSPELL, Code Africa or the STEM Kids Championship gives students a goal to work toward and a reason to take the club seriously.
AFRISTEM works with schools to introduce or strengthen STEM programmes, activities and learning experiences. If you would like support, reach out through our Schools page.

news.title: 10 STEM Careers Africa Urgently Needs More Of
news.excerpt: From renewable-energy engineers to data scientists and biomedical researchers — a look at the STEM careers that will shape Africa's next decade.
news.author: AFRISTEM Team
body: Africa's challenges — in energy, health, agriculture, infrastructure and finance — are also its greatest opportunities. Every one of them needs STEM talent.

Renewable-energy engineers, software developers, data scientists, agricultural scientists, biomedical researchers, cybersecurity specialists, environmental scientists, robotics engineers, chemical engineers and mathematics educators are all in growing demand.
The good news: the foundations for every one of these careers are laid in primary and secondary school. Curiosity, problem-solving and a love of learning matter more than any single subject.
AFRISTEM programmes are designed to spark those foundations early, so that today's competitors become tomorrow's professionals.

news.title: Student Story: 'The Tournament Made Me Fall in Love With Chemistry'
news.excerpt: A senior secondary student shares how preparing for the African Organic Chemistry Tournament changed how she sees science — and her future.
news.author: AFRISTEM Team
body: "Before the tournament, organic chemistry was just diagrams I had to memorise. Preparing for it changed everything — I started to see the logic, the patterns, the beauty in how molecules behave."
Months of preparation with her chemistry teacher and classmates turned into hours of focused problem-solving on tournament day. She did not win first place. She says it did not matter.
"I discovered I could think through a hard problem without panicking. I discovered I actually enjoy it. Now I want to study chemical engineering."
Stories like hers are why the African Organic Chemistry Tournament exists: not only to identify the best, but to inspire everyone who takes part.

faqs.question: Who can participate in AFRISTEM programmes?
faqs.answer: AFRISTEM programmes vary by age and category. Each programme page clearly states its eligibility requirements — from primary school learners in the STEM Kids Championship to senior secondary students in the African Organic Chemistry Tournament.

faqs.question: How do I register for an AFRISTEM programme?
faqs.answer: Visit the Registration page and complete the relevant form. Some programmes may have specific registration requirements or windows, which are stated on each programme page.

faqs.question: Can schools register their students?
faqs.answer: Yes. Where applicable, schools can register students for AFRISTEM programmes and competitions. Bulk school registration is available on the Registration page.

faqs.question: Are AFRISTEM programmes available online?
faqs.answer: Some programmes may be offered online, physically or in hybrid formats depending on the programme. Our teacher hangouts, for example, are fully virtual.

faqs.question: Can my school partner with AFRISTEM?
faqs.answer: Yes. AFRISTEM welcomes partnerships with schools and educational institutions for competitions, STEM clubs, training, boot camps, equipment and consultancy.

faqs.question: Can educators participate?
faqs.answer: Yes. Educators can participate in teacher training, workshops, professional development, and can serve as facilitators, judges, mentors and programme coordinators.

faqs.question: Can STEM professionals volunteer?
faqs.answer: Yes. STEM professionals can participate as mentors, facilitators, trainers, speakers, judges, consultants, project advisers or industry partners.

faqs.question: Does AFRISTEM sell STEM equipment?
faqs.answer: Yes. AFRISTEM provides STEM equipment, educational kits and learning resources, and can support institutions in setting up practical STEM learning environments.

faqs.question: Does AFRISTEM provide certificates?
faqs.answer: Certificates are provided for programmes where certification is applicable. Details are stated on the individual programme page.

faqs.question: Can organisations partner with AFRISTEM?
faqs.answer: Yes. We welcome partnerships with organisations that share our commitment to STEM education, innovation, technology and youth development.

faqs.question: How can I contact AFRISTEM?
faqs.answer: You can reach us through the Contact page using the enquiry form, by phone or WhatsApp, or via the official contact channels listed on this website.
